title: Eye for Eye
lead: "Eye for eye, tooth for tooth" (Exodus 21:24; Leviticus 24:20; Deuteronomy 19:21) limited revenge to a fair measure. The rabbis read it as monetary compensation, and Jesus answered it with "do not set yourself against the evil person" (Matthew 5:38–42).

sections.b: The rule appears three times in the Torah, each in a different setting: injuries in a fight (Exodus 21:23–25), injury to a neighbor in the Holiness Code, with one law for the foreigner and the native (Leviticus 24:17–22), and the punishment of a false witness (Deuteronomy 19:16–21). Older laws such as Hammurabi's also used it. Proverbs warns against private revenge (Proverbs 20:22; Proverbs 24:29), and Jesus answers the saying in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:38–42; Luke 6:29). Paul tells believers not to repay evil for evil, while saying that rulers bear the sword (Romans 12:17–13:4).
